items.name: Scene heading
items.description: Slug line opening each scene: INT. or EXT., the place, and the time of day, all capitals. Indents are measured from the left page edge on US Letter.

rules.scene_number_position: optional, both margins in shooting scripts

items.name: Action
items.description: Description of what is seen and heard, written in present tense, full text width, sentence case, single spaced.
examples: Two kids run across the empty playground.

items.name: Character
items.description: Speaker's name in capitals above their dialogue, with extensions such as V.O., O.S. and CONT'D in brackets after it.

items.name: Dialogue
items.description: Spoken words directly under the character name, sentence case, in a narrower centred column about 3.5 in wide.
examples: I told you we shouldn't come here.

items.name: Parenthetical
items.description: Short direction in brackets on its own line between character and dialogue, lower case, used sparingly.

items.name: Shot
items.description: Optional line naming a camera shot or angle, capitals, full width, set like a scene heading but within a scene. Not a Fountain element; written as a forced scene heading or action line.

items.name: Transition
items.description: Instruction for moving between scenes, capitals, aligned to the right side of the text area, followed by a colon except for a few such as FADE OUT.

items.name: Centered text
items.description: Text centred between the margins, in capitals, typically for titles such as THE END.

items.name: Capitalisation rules
items.description: Which parts are written in capitals: scene headings entirely, character names every time, transitions and shot lines entirely; a character's first appearance in action is also capitalised. Dialogue, parentheticals and normal action stay in sentence case. Sound cues may also be capitalised in action.

rules.action: sentence case; character name uppercase on first introduction
rules.extension_format: (V.O.) (O.S.) (CONT'D) uppercase in brackets after the name

items.name: Common transitions
items.description: Frequently used transitions. Modern specs use them sparingly, since editing choices usually belong to the director.

rules.line_ending: colon, except FADE OUT. and FADE IN: which follow their own punctuation

items.name: US Letter page
items.description: US Letter page setup: Courier 12 pt (10 characters per inch), 6 lines per inch, one-inch top and bottom margins, wide left margin for binding. About one page per minute of screen time.

rules.page_number_position: top right, about 0.5 in from top, followed by a period

items.name: A4 page
items.description: A4 variant for UK and international use. Same font and margins as Letter; the page is narrower and taller, so the text block is about 5.77 in wide and holds more lines. Derived by applying the Letter margins to A4 dimensions (6 lines per inch over 9.69 in); no single authority publishes A4 margins.

rules.note: element indents stay as on Letter; lines_per_page derived

items.name: MORE and CONT'D
items.description: When dialogue is split across pages, end the page with (MORE) in the dialogue column and repeat the character name with (CONT'D) at the top of the next. (CONT'D) is also added when the same character speaks again after an action line. Never leave a scene heading alone at the page bottom, and avoid splitting a short action paragraph or a single dialogue line.

items.name: Scene numbers
items.description: Optional. Numbers appear in shooting scripts or when requested, on both left and right of the scene heading, and are locked once drafts circulate; inserted scenes take letters (12A). Spec scripts omit them.

items.name: Title page
items.description: Title page is unnumbered and holds the title centred about a third down the page, a by-line and contact details bottom left. Page 1 of the script follows and is not numbered visibly.

items.name: Fountain: scene heading
items.description: A line starting with INT, EXT, EST, INT./EXT, INT/EXT or I/E is read as a scene heading. A leading period forces one. A scene number goes in hashes at the end.

items.name: Fountain: action
items.description: Any paragraph that fits no other element. A leading exclamation mark forces action; tabs and spaces are kept.

items.name: Fountain: character
items.description: A line in capitals with a blank line above and text below. Extensions go in brackets. An at-sign forces a mixed-case name. A caret after the second name makes dual dialogue.

items.name: Fountain: dialogue
items.description: Text directly following a character or parenthetical line, with no blank line between.

items.name: Fountain: parenthetical
items.description: A line wrapped in brackets between character and dialogue.
examples:
STEEL
(starting the engine)
Here we go.

items.name: Fountain: transition
items.description: A capitals line ending in TO: with blank lines around it. A leading > forces any transition.

items.name: Fountain: centered text
items.description: Text wrapped in > and <, spaces optional.

items.name: Fountain: other markup
items.description: Page break is three or more equals signs alone; sections start with #; synopses with =; lyrics with ~; notes sit in double square brackets; boneyard (omitted text) in slash-star. Emphasis: *italic*, **bold**, ***both***, _underline_.

items.name: Fountain: title page
items.description: Key: value pairs at the top of the file, ended by a blank line.

rules.keys: Title, Credit, Author, Source, Draft date, Contact

examples:
Title: Playground
Credit: Written by
Author: A. Writer
Draft date: 2026-10-15
